Medication & toxin exposure: “Any over‑the‑counter meds, antacids, diuretics, laxatives, alcohol, methanol, ethylene glycol?” — Antacids → alkalosis; diuretics → alkalosis; toxins → high‑anion‑gap acidosis.
| Metabolic alkalosis (vomiting) | Persistent vomiting, nasogastric suction, antacid overuse | Low Cl⁻, high HCO₃⁻, paradoxical aciduria |

Medication / supplements: Use of antacids, PPIs, iron chelators, chronic NSAIDs, anti‑malarial prophylaxis. — Reduced gastric acidity or drug‑induced GI bleeding impair iron absorption or increase loss.
| Peptic ulcer disease / perforated ulcer | Epigastric pain related to meals, melena, free air on X‑ray | Pain relieved by antacids, no lipase elevation, pneumoperitoneum on imaging |

Medication / supplement: Current drugs (thiazides, lithium, bisphosphonates, calcimimetics), calcium or vitamin D intake, antacids — Certain agents raise calcium or suppress PTH; others lower calcium.

qs.q: What is a primary limitation associated with the long-term regular use of aluminum-containing antacids in pediatric patients?
qs.e: Aluminum antacids are associated with constipation, whereas magnesium antacids commonly cause diarrhea. Tardive dyskinesia is a recognized warning linked to chronic use of metoclopramide.
